final_candidates.decision_summary: Conservative hydrophobic substitution in the HA1 stem with strong PLM plausibility (z=0.620) and high structure compatibility (z=0.931). Away from receptor-binding and fusion machinery, so folding stability gains should preserve entry.

Perfect PLM plausibility (z=1.000) with high structure compatibility (z=0.972) and decent MSA tolerance. Surface position distal to RBD and fusion peptide; charge-conserving substitution keeps function intact.

Highest structure compatibility in the pool (z=0.983) with solid MSA support; beta-branched isoleucine in a buried hydrophobic position is a classic thermostabilizing move. PLM support is modest but acceptable.

stop_reason.detail: Evidence across MSA, PLM, and structure tools has converged on a stable Top-3 and no phenotype predictor is available, so further rounds would not change the outcome.

history.rationale: Conservative hydrophobic core packing change in the HA1 distal domain, far from receptor-binding and cleavage sites; Ile often increases folded-state packing stability.
Highest MSA mutant frequency but weakest structure compatibility (0.48); retained but demoted.
Structure compatibility z=0.483 is notably lower than the leaders, and MSA/PLM support is only modest. Retained as backup but demoted below L57I.
MSA and structure scores are moderate while PLM plausibility is low, keeping this as a lower-ranked backup candidate. No further re-ranking until additional evidence arrives.
Internal Leu-to-Ile substitution in the HA1 stem-adjacent region that can improve core packing without perturbing surface epitopes or functional sites.
Best structural compatibility (0.98) and observed in homologs, but weak ESM-1v score lowers overall confidence; core Leu→Ile can enhance packing.
Highest structure compatibility score among all candidates and decent evolutionary tolerance. Leu→Ile in a buried context is a classic thermostability move; PLM is weaker but not disqualifying.

Highest structure compatibility in the pool (z=0.983) with solid MSA and PLM support; beta-branched isoleucine is a classic thermostabilizing substitution in buried hydrophobic cores. Retained at rank 3 pending any further structural evidence.
Stem-region (HA1 C-terminal, pre-cleavage-site) valine to isoleucine; the HA stem tolerates conservative hydrophobic substitutions and added buried volume can stabilize the trimer.
Moderate structure compatibility but low MSA applicability (0.60) and no PLM support; kept on the bubble.
Good structure compatibility but weak MSA applicability (0.60) and coverage-limited homolog support. Kept as fifth candidate; unlikely to enter Top-3.
Structure compatibility is high (z=0.767) but MSA and PLM both weakly disfavor this position. Retained only as a low-priority candidate pending stronger evidence.
Another stem-region conservative hydrophobic substitution that may increase buried packing interactions while lying outside the KRRKR cleavage motif and fusion peptide.

Best combination of ESM-1v plausibility (0.62) and strong structural compatibility (0.93) despite low natural frequency; isoleucine packs well in hydrophobic cores and is a classic stabilizing substitution.

Consistent support across all three informative tools: MSA tolerance, strong PLM plausibility, and high structure compatibility. Hydrophobic core-adjacent isoleucine substitution plausibly improves thermostability without affecting receptor-binding or cleavage sites.

Consistent support across all three informative tools: MSA tolerance (z=0.006 close to WT preference but I is a conservative substitution), strongest PLM plausibility among retained structural candidates, and high structure compatibility. V328 sits in the HA1 stem region away from receptor-binding sites, so folding stability gain with preserved entry function is plausible.
HA2 helical core Leu-to-Ile change away from the fusion peptide and disulfide network; conservative substitutions here are generally tolerated and can enhance thermal stability.
Zero MSA frequency and essentially zero PLM plausibility; I is never seen at 446.

rejection.reason: Zero MSA frequency and essentially zero PLM plausibility; I is never seen at 446.

history.rationale: Proline in the HA2 lower stem can rigidify local backbone and is a common stabilizing motif in HA engineering; must verify no functional constraint at this position.
Zero MSA support and lowest PLM score; proline at 496 risks disturbing the region despite proline's general rigidity benefit.

rejection.reason: Zero MSA support and lowest PLM score; proline at 496 risks disturbing the region despite proline's general rigidity benefit.

history.rationale: Surface-conservative charge-preserving substitution in the HA1 head region; low functional risk and possible modest improvement of local H-bond/salt-bridge network.
Highest PLM plausibility and strong structure compatibility with E present in homologs; conservative charge-preserving substitution near the disulfide-rich region.

Maximal PLM plausibility (z=1.000) and high structural compatibility; charge-conservative E substitution at a surface position is stability-neutral to positive. Slight caution because MSA frequency is modest, so confidences of the top two are effectively tied.

Perfect PLM plausibility (z=1.000), high structure compatibility (z=0.972), and decent MSA support; elevated from rank 2 to reflect the combined evidence strength. Position 46 is on the HA1 surface distal from the fusion peptide and receptor-binding domain, so charge retention keeps entry function intact.
